title: Angular Essentials
description: Angular's CLI, core packages, and RxJS — and how modern standalone components reduce NgModule boilerplate.

data.text: Angular is a batteries-included platform: a single CLI scaffolds apps, and `@angular/*` packages cover rendering, routing, forms, and HTTP. Unlike React, you rarely pick and choose an ecosystem — the framework ships the pieces.

data.title: Create an Angular application
data.content: The CLI is run through npx so a global install is optional.
data.code:
npx -p @angular/cli@latest ng new my-app --standalone --style=scss --routing
cd my-app
npm start

rows: Reactive streams used throughout the framework

data.caption: src/app/user-card.component.ts — standalone component with signals

data.text: Standalone components declare their own imports and replace `NgModule` boilerplate. Angular recommends them for all new code; the dependency-injection system and RxJS remain central either way.

data.title: Do not mix package versions
data.text: All `@angular/*` packages and the CLI must share a major version, and the build toolchain (`@angular-devkit/build-angular`) follows the same release train. Angular's `ng update` command updates them together and runs migration schematics.

data.title: Upgrade Angular packages safely
data.code:
npx ng update @angular/core @angular/cli
npx ng update            # shows what else is available

terms.definition: The ng command for scaffolding, building, testing, and upgrading Angular projects.
A component that declares its own imports without belonging to an NgModule.
Angular's reactive primitive (signal, computed, effect) introduced to simplify change detection.
The reactive-streams library Angular uses for HTTP, events, and async state.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Explain dependency injection and change detection, and note that modern Angular favours standalone components and signals over NgModules and manual subscriptions.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: The Angular CLI owns scaffolding, building, testing, and upgrades.
Official @angular/* packages are versioned and released together.
Standalone components remove most NgModule boilerplate.
Signals and RxJS coexist — signals for state, RxJS for async streams.
data.takeaway: Angular's opinionated, all-in-one design is the key contrast with React and Vue.
